content: Copper: From past to present For thousands of years, copper has been so widespread that most people encounter it without even noticing. Ancient Egyptians used copper to disinfect wounds and surgical tools, and the earliest copper alloy weaponry dates back to the mid-5th millennium B.C. From building tools to biology and biotechnology, copper is an essential part of human life. Do you know as human beings, we need 1.2 milligrams of copper daily to help enzymes transfer energy inside our cells. Multi-utility Copper Nearly 70 percent of worldwide copper produced is used for electrical and communication purposes. The other applications include transportation, cookware, catalysts and as a micro-nutrient in food and animal feed. As per an estimation in the last one hundred years, 690 million tonnes of copper has been produced and two-thirds of it is still in productive use. Copper: an eco-friendly material As the world celebrates World Earth Day, the significance of copper recycling needs to be looked into and understood. Copper recycling plays a crucial role in promoting sustainability. Let’s explore why copper is such an eco-friendly material Infinite Recyclability Copper is a 100% recyclable material with an infinite life cycle. When a copper product reaches the end of its useful life, it can be recovered, melted down, and cast into a new product without any loss of its chemical or physical properties. This recyclability ensures that copper can be used over and over again, reducing the need for new mining and extraction. Reduced Carbon Emissions Recycling scrap copper produces fewer carbon emissions compared to mining virgin copper. By opting for recycling, we can minimize air pollution and contribute to a cleaner environment Preserving Natural Resources Recycling copper helps preserve the earth’s natural resources. Instead of extracting new copper from mines, we can reuse existing copper, thereby conserving valuable resources for future generations. Supporting Jobs The scrap metal recycling sector relies on copper recycling. By participating in this process, we not only contribute to sustainability but also support jobs in the recycling industry. Circular Economy Copper is a key player in the circular economy. Circular systems maximize the potential of sustainable materials, reduce waste, and lower greenhouse gas emissions. Copper applications, such as renewable energy systems, energy-efficient buildings, and smart grid technologies, enable the green transition. By choosing recycled copper, companies contribute to a circular economy, minimizing their carbon footprint and promoting responsible resource management.
